title: Mike Kelley: Materialist Aesthetics and Memory Illusions

description.main: A critical study of Mike Kelley's art and writing as a position in materialist aesthetics, by Laura López Paniagua, with an introduction by John Miller.
description.extended:
A scholarly study that reads Mike Kelley's art and writing as a position in materialist aesthetics.

Laura López Paniagua reads Kelley alongside Bataille, Benjamin, Bourdieu, Freud, Lacan and Merleau-Ponty. The book concentrates on his writing about the aesthetics of the 1980s to the 2000s and on his treatment of victim culture and repressed memory syndrome. John Miller contributes an introduction. The argument treats his critique and his statements as part of the work itself, so that Kelley appears as something close to an empirical philosopher who made his case through art as well as essays. Mousse Publishing issued the paperback at 244 pages, with 34 color and 53 black-and-white illustrations.

Kelley (1954 to 2012) was an American artist who wrote on culture and politics alongside his art. López Paniagua completed a doctoral thesis on memory in his work in 2015, and this is her first monograph.

notes: Distributed in North America by D.A.P. from March 2021.
